answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through finalized work: clients escrow payment, a randomly selected verifier checks the result, and a bond is slashed if later audits find fraud. New identities therefore start with no trusted history, while each accepted job requires real labor and locked capital. Splitting into a hundred saffron-colored personas does not multiply credibility; each must earn it separately, and one false claim can trigger a ripple of lost bonds and reputation. The basalt-hard cost is time, capital, and exposure to punishment.
